_doc: THE canonical runner config (nb-ci controller, scripts/ci/mini-runner-labels.sh, tests). Isolation: auto repos (NB_CI_MODE=auto, repo variable overrides org) route to nb-auto / nb-deploy / nb-ctl, labels no legacy runner carries; legacy repos keep runner-vm / nb-route on today's runners, so neither side can take the other's jobs. One ephemeral VM per job, first class whose labels contain all of the job's labels. The fallback runner gets fallback_labels ADDED (its own labels untouched) only while GCP cannot start VMs. Mac Mini CI labels (ci_labels) are removed only after every repo is auto. 2026-11-27: Mac Minis removed from CI; legacy lanes are served by classes legacy/legacy-prod, nb-route by the controller's nb-ctl runners.

classes.name: control
classes._doc: route + notify jobs of auto repos (runs-on nb-ctl): the 2 runners on the always-on controller VM, no VM boot

classes.name: deploy
classes._doc: build + rsync / S3 release: standard VM, a preemption can never leave a partial deploy

classes.name: gate
classes._doc: fastest 8-vCPU Spot type the quota allows (us-central1 quotas 2026-11-27: C3 24, N2D 16, C2D 100): c2d-highcpu-8 so 32 vCPU = 4 concurrent jobs; change machine/vcpu/ram_gb/price here only. sa=ro: read-only npm-cache bucket token

classes.name: legacy
classes._doc: Legacy lanes (repos not on NB_CI_MODE=auto), packed (2026-11-27, Pulse 652ffcd8). nb-route: a free slot of a live packed VM also takes route/notify/Gate-summary jobs (curl/jq, the same secrets the slot's deploy jobs already get), so they never queue behind the 2 controller runners; class_for still maps a bare nb-route job to 'control', so it never buys a VM.8 one-job runner slots per e2-standard-8 Spot VM (was 4 per e2-standard-4 until 2026-11-27 09:00: external IPs, 8 per region, were the cap, not vCPU; same 1 vCPU + 4 GB per slot, half the IPs), each its own user/HOME/work dir/private /tmp, no sudo; the VM is reused while jobs flow and deleted after 3 min idle (hard lifetime 4 h). Measured: a job VM averaged 27% of 4 vCPU (p90 62%), so 4 jobs fill one VM; 3 VMs = 24 slots on 3 IPs inside 32 vCPU / 8 IPs less the controller, deploy VMs and the AQA reserve.

classes.name: legacy-prod
classes._doc: Legacy jobs that ask for lane-prod/lane-dev (deploy lanes): standard VM, never preempted mid-deploy. Never packed: a deploy job (prod secrets) never shares or reuses a VM that ran PR code.

prices_usd._doc: GCP Cloud Billing Catalog, us-central1, read 2026-11-26 (services/6F81-5844-456A). Per hour unless noted.

fallback._doc: No fallback runner: nb-ci never hands CI labels to a Mac Mini (user order 2026-11-27). GCP refusing VMs = jobs wait + Pulse alert.

quota._doc: One budget for CI + AutoQA: deploy > gate > AutoQA. Gate VMs leave reserve_deploy_vcpu free; AutoQA gets what is left (published as project metadata nb-autoqa-vcpu-allowance). reserve_aqa: CI scale-up (computed from live CPUS_ALL_REGIONS / CPUS / IN_USE_ADDRESSES / INSTANCES / SSD_TOTAL_GB usage) always leaves one AQA VM (2 vCPU e2-standard-2 + 1 external IP; AQA stays that size while CI waits) free, less what live aqa-* VMs already hold.
